outcomes.text: Find the lexical verb and separate the subject from the immediate parts of the basic VP.
Compare six verb patterns by the number and functions of their complements.
Explain what a predicative describes and distinguish a PP complement from an optional location.

opening.prompt: Which word is the main verb in “The wind shook the shutters”?

options.feedback: “Wind” is the noun in the subject.
“Shook” names the action and heads the VP.
“Shutters” is the noun in the object.

opening.prompt: In “Eli packed the red bag”, which whole group answers “What did Eli pack?”

options.feedback: Include the words that go with the noun in the object.
That span also contains the verb.
All three words belong to the object NP.

opening.prompt: Who receives something in “The courier gave Ada a receipt”?

options.feedback: Ada receives the receipt.
The courier gives the receipt.
A receipt is what is given.

opening.prompt: What is quiet in “The librarian kept the room quiet”?

options.feedback: The description applies to the space the librarian kept quiet.
“Quiet” describes “the room”.

options.text: Both the librarian and the room
options.feedback: The sentence describes the room and leaves the librarian’s own noise level open.

opening.prompt: In “The visitors rested near the gate”, which group can be removed while keeping the same action and a complete sentence?

options.feedback: Those words supply the subject.
The sentence needs this verb to express the action.
“The visitors rested” already expresses a complete action. The PP adds its location.

closing.prompt: Compare “The bell rang” and “The caretaker rang the bell”. Which groups are the two VPs, in that order?

options.feedback: Those are the subjects. Find the verb in each sentence.
The first VP has no complement. The second contains the direct object “the bell”.
“The bell” is the second sentence’s object. The VP includes its verb as well.

closing.prompt: In “Ari sent a note to Ren”, what are the roles of “a note” and “to Ren”, in that order?

options.feedback: Ren is the recipient. The note is the thing sent.
“To Ren” identifies the recipient in this two-complement pattern.

options.text: Direct object and recipient expressed as a PP
options.feedback: “A note” is the thing sent, and “to Ren” expresses the recipient in PP form.

closing.prompt: In “Nia became a pilot”, what function does “a pilot” have?

options.feedback: “A pilot” identifies Nia after the change.
The NP identifies the subject in this pattern.
This sentence describes a change in Nia’s role. There is no recipient.

closing.prompt: In “The team painted the door blue”, what does “blue” do inside the VP?

options.feedback: The sentence says what colour the door became.
“Blue” is an object predicative. It describes the direct object “the door”.
“The door” is what the team painted. “Blue” gives the resulting colour.

closing.prompt: In “The recipe consists of three steps”, what role does “of three steps” play?

options.feedback: The PP identifies what makes up the recipe. It gives no place.
The preposition “of” heads a PP that this use of “consists” selects.
“Consists” selects an “of” phrase here to specify the parts of the recipe.
